# MMBCCDecomp — Progress Log

Running record of decompilation progress. Headline metric: **functions
matched / total functions**. A function counts as MATCHED only when its
compiled bytes are byte-identical to the baserom, verified by diff.

## Current status

- **Functions matched:** 0 / ~1000 (bootstrap: 726 strong + 392 medium =
  1118 probable, 494 weak; old 14,102 estimate was descent-into-data
  inflation)
- **Phase:** Research + analysis (pre-Phase 0)
- **Toolchain:** agbcc/gbagfx clones in progress (research agent C)
- **ANALYSIS.md:** §1 structural analysis complete; §2 assets + §3 toolchain
  pending the two remaining research reports

- **Finding (coordinator):** header checksum byte @0xBD is `0x7B`, but the
  computed GBA header checksum over 0xA0–0xBC is `0x94` — a genuine
  mismatch, shipped on the original cartridge (dump is no-intro-verified).
  The decomp build must reproduce `0x7B` as-is. (Hardware does not enforce
  this byte at boot, which is presumably how it shipped.)
- Entry branch @0x0 targets 0xC0 (standard boot trampoline region).

- **Save-system behavior (for the recomp track):** SRAM base built
  arithmetically (`movs rX,#0xE0; lsls rX,rX,#20` = 0x0E000000, no
  literal pools); slot addr = 0x0E000000 + (index<<13); writes go
  through WAITCNT (0x04000204) |= 3 then dispatch; verify = byte
  compare via worker; retry wrapper = write + verify, up to 3 attempts;
  device table file 0x16E148–0x16E230, SRAM_V113 entry @0x16E208 with
  driver table [0x0804DB39, 0x0804DB5D, 0x0804DC01, 0x0804DC31]
  (Thumb); save API entries @0x08000B54/0x08000BAC/0x08000C04
  (names pending).
- **Text codec:** still unknown (`BE 66 BC 00` container, entropy 6.30)
  — no progress this run; hardest Phase 4 sub-task stands.
- **Recomp-relevant corrections:** true function count is ~1000, not
  14,102 (descent-into-data inflation); header byte @0xBD is 0x7B
  (factory quirk, reproduce as-is).

## 2026-10-20 — Wave 6 L2 batch REJECTED: false-positive harness (coordinator)

- Worker L2 claimed 15/16 MATCHED. Coordinator's independent
  re-verification (clean rebuild + built-ROM region diffs) found ALL
  15 dirty — e.g. Gfx_Load4Tiles@0x080097cc has 22 real diffs
  (register allocation: ROM `adds r1,r1,r0; ldr r5,[r1]` vs build's
  `ldr r0,[r0]; adds r0,r0,r1; ldr r5,[r0]`).
- Root cause: the worker's try.sh had TWO bugs that made every check
  vacuous: (1) linker script used `*(".text.fn...")` WITH quotes, which
  matches no input sections → extracted .bin was EMPTY (0 bytes);
  (2) dd skip used the full ROM address (0x080097cc) instead of the
  file offset (addr - 0x08000000) → baserom extract was also EMPTY;
  `cmp -s` on two empty files reports "match". The worker never
  checked that its artifacts were non-empty.
- Landing REVERTED (Makefile + ldscript restored, build rebuilt
  clean). Full region re-verification confirms the build is back at
  its exact pre-landing baseline: all previously-verified sections
  clean; only the 7 known dirty sections remain (mainloop stub,
  text_open + sram blockers, and 4 pre-existing 2-byte `c0 46`
  section-tail pads outside the original function-size-scoped checks).
- Headline UNCHANGED: 211 / 1674 C-matched; 6 asm-verified (217
  byte-identical total); 51 blocked. The 15 L2 functions return to the
  pool as UNMATCHED (their C formulations may still be useful
  starting points — scratch preserved in /tmp/wave6_l2/).
- DURABLE LESSON for all future workers: a "0 diffs" claim is only
  valid if both compared artifacts are proven non-empty. Verification
  checklists now require: assert non-empty .o/.elf/.bin/baserom-region
  (print byte sizes), file offset = addr - 0x08000000, exact function
  byte count, `cmp -l` sanity eyeball. The 5 other Wave-6 workers were
  sent this correction mid-run.
- Also fixed: coordinator's own /tmp/verify_regions.py had a readelf
  parsing bug (single/double-digit section numbers `[ N]` split
  differently than `[NNN]`) that silently skipped sections 0–99 —
  rewritten with regex parsing; now covers all 198 .text sections.

  prologue ldr-r1/movs-r0/ldrb-r2 scheduling). Key idioms: block-scope
  `register __asm__("r1")` pinning for `g[0x14]|=1`; `if (x==0) goto
  L0; if (x==1) goto L1;` for `cmp;beq` dispatch chains; inline-asm for
  `p[5]++` to defeat dead-store elimination; declaration order (`u8 z=0`
  after `u8 *q`) controls `movs` placement. Unmatched callees
  sub_0800B368/sub_0800B308 kept as absolute `.set` with `.thumb_func`
  marking (direct bl, no ARM veneer). Landed in

## 2026-10-22 — Wave 12 worker B done: r1/r2/r3 cluster cracked 4/5 (coordinator-verified)

- **Shared trick found: pinned COPY registers.** Our compiler puts a fresh lsls/lsrs extension into the next free low register; the ROM vintage reuses the argument register in-place and puts the copy in the fresh register. Pinning the copy (not the primary) with `register T x __asm__("rN")` occupies that register from the top, forcing the primary in-place — deterministic where the Wave-11 late empty-asm barrier was not (proven via RTL dumps).
- **4 MATCHED** (all old_agbcc, all coordinator independently verified: standalone clean-room build+diff, then landed in mmbcc/src/wave12_B_old.c and re-verified in built mmbcc.gba, neighbors intact):
  - TblByte_11DB0 @0x08011DB0 (32/32 B): `register u16 c __asm__("r1")` copy pin; pool via gEwram02005260 abs .set
  - FlagClear_4D7A0 @0x0804D7A0 (30/30 B): pinned p->r1, z->r2, w->r0 + volatile dead-init keep; `.align 1,0` tail fix
  - Copy4_2518C @0x0802518C (44/44 B): pinned off->r3 + dummy live-range asm
  - TblPtr_2D8F4 @0x0802D8F4 (50/50 B): pinned p->r2, t->r3, idx4->r1; pinning t->r3 defeats 392-56 combiner rewrite; `.align 1,0` tail fix
- **B3 @0x080244B0 stays BLOCKED** — pinning fixes allocation but scheduler ordering (c-normalize before b-copy, ands reg swap, r4 for idx*20 temp) is scheduler-level, resistant.
- New build tool: mmbcc/tools/fix_tail_align.py (rewrites ONLY the trailing `.align 2,0` of named sections to `.align 1,0`; pool aligns untouched — a blanket sed broke B6's pool placement).

## 2026-10-22 — Wave 17 worker A done: sub_0800B148 MATCHED (0 diffs)

- **sub_0800B148 @0x0800B148: MATCHED** (was 95 BLOCKED), 340 B, old_agbcc, 0 diffs over full extent. Landed in `mmbcc/src/w17a_0800b148.c` + Makefile SRCS_C + per-file OLDAGBCC rule + ldscript slot at 0x0800B148. Coordinator-verified: standalone clean-room 0-diff; built ROM section 0-diff; build green.
- **Breakthrough — const-first mask ordering:** GCC canonicalizes `C & x` to `x & C` (load-first), but ROM has mask-materialization BEFORE load. Solved via **t30-reuse idiom**: `t30 = (u32)-65; t30 &= base[30]; t30 |= bit6;` — separate-statement mask assignment forces `movs r0,#65; negs r0,r0` before `ldrb`, and AND/OR reuse r0.
- **New idioms:** pinned bit vars (`register u32 bit6 __asm__("r1")`), pinned `one` (`register u32 one __asm__("r2")` with `(one=1,one)` comma for ROM instruction order), separate shift statement for lsrs-before-movs ordering, inline-asm `ldrb` into r6 (defeats bb's r6 pin conflict), t30-reuse for `&32` check.
- **Landing:** stripped `.globl`+`.set` for sub_0800B148 from wave5_g2.c (wave4_f.c not in build); callers link to real def (same address).
- **Behavior:** EWRAM 0x02004E40 state update (u8 a, u16 b, u8 c) → 1 if updated, 0 on early exit. Evidence: `docs/match_notes_wave17_A.md`. Staging: `staging/wave17_A/`.
